sentences.text: In the meantime, if so advised, the petitioner may file a response to the interlocutory application.

7. On the merits of the case, learned counsel for the petitioners has submitted that the petitioners are aggrieved by the fact that the District Land Acquisition Officer has included certain persons as legal heirs and successors of the recorded tenant for the purposes of disbursement of compensation and as per the Hindu Succession Act, they are not entitled.

He submits that those persons have been made party respondents in the present case as 5 and 6.
8.

Learned counsel for the respondents submits that in case of any dispute with regards to the legal heirs and successors and consequent entitlement of any portion of the compensation, the reference has to be made to the court under Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
He has also submitted that petitioners have filed a petition vide Annexure-3 before the District Land Acquisition Officer, though the petition ought to have been filed before the Deputy Collector.
The learned counsel submits that if a fresh petition is filed before the Deputy Collector, the same can still be referred to Court under Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act.
He also submits that the matter regarding succession cannot be decided in writ jurisdiction and the petitioners have appropriate remedy under the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act itself.

(Anubha Rawat Choudhary, J.) Binit Kalyani Mahatowin And Others vs The State Of Jharkhand And Others on 16 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171206194/
